strengths: Clear binary form with proper repeat signs and balanced 8+8 phrase structure
Correct baroque harmonic progression with functional circle-of-fifths motion in second strain
Bass line provides basic harmonic foundation with root-position triads
issues: Treble voice lacks baroque melodic elegance: consecutive eighth-note pairs create mechanical ostinato rather than graceful minuet gesture (mm.1-2, 5-6)
Bass is entirely quarter-note roots with no rhythmic variety, voice-leading, or characteristic baroque bass patterns like Alberti or walking motion

Missing essential baroque features: no cadential trills, no six-four cadential embellishments, no melodic ornamentation, and parallel fifths implied between voices on beat 3 of mm.1-2 (G-D in treble over G-B in bass)
suggestions: Revise treble to include more stepwise motion and characteristic minuet upbeat-downbeat patterns, e.g., B4 c2 | d2 Bd gd for mm.1
Add rhythmic variety to bass: use broken chord figuration or at least a quarter-eighth pattern like G,3 B,2 | D,3 F,2 to support the 3/4 meter gracefully
Insert a cadential six-four and trill at the half-cadence in m.4 and authentic cadence in m.8, e.g., treble c2 B2 A2 | G4 z2 with bass D,2 G,2 D,2 | G,4 z2
critic.summary: A harmonically competent but mechanically rendered minuet that satisfies formal requirements while failing to capture baroque elegance; the treble's repetitive paired-eighth figuration and the bass's inert quarter-note roots produce a pedagogical exercise rather than a graceful dance movement.
